skill.name: explain-codebase
skill.description: Build an onboarding map of an unfamiliar repository covering purpose, entry points, how to run it, main modules, data flow and risky areas, with file references. Use when asked to explain, map or onboard onto a codebase.
skill.summary: Create a concise, file-referenced onboarding map covering repository structure, setup, data flow, dependencies, and uncertainties.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: Eight findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, read-only history inspection, citation rules, or explicit secret protections. One finding is confirmed because the skill directs execution of unfamiliar repository tests and lint commands without requiring review or isolation. No evidence found of data exfiltration, destructive intent, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:17 directs execution of repository-defined tests and lint commands without a trust check.
remediation.suggestion: Review command definitions and hooks before execution, obtain approval, and isolate untrusted commands without credentials or unnecessary network access.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories make it difficult to find entry points, setup steps, and important dependencies. This skill guides a file-referenced onboarding map with one traced flow and clear open questions.
actual_capabilities: Summarize repository purpose and intended users from project documentation.
Identify setup, run, and test commands, distinguishing verified commands from unverified ones.
Map two directory levels, languages, frameworks, and application entry points.
Trace one central request, command, or event through files and functions.
Describe data models, configuration variable names, and external service integrations.
Highlight tests, CI checks, maintenance signals, reading priorities, and open questions with file references.
limitations: Requires access to repository files and suitable host tools; it includes no standalone analysis program.
Covers selected files and one central flow, not every execution path or architectural detail.
Cannot verify setup or test behavior when commands are unavailable, unsafe, or not executed.
Identifies quality signals but does not provide a comprehensive security audit or guarantee correctness.

use_cases.title: Orient a New Developer
use_cases.description: Find setup steps, entry points, and three useful files to read before starting a first contribution.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Technical Handoff
use_cases.description: Summarize module responsibilities, external dependencies, and unresolved questions for a team taking ownership.

use_cases.title: Plan an Integration Investigation
use_cases.description: Trace a central request through application layers and identify configuration names and service boundaries relevant to an integration.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Get Oriented
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this repository in one page. Cover its purpose, directory map, entry points, and three files to read first. Cite files you inspect.
prompt_templates.scenario: First review of an unfamiliar repository

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Understand Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Map setup, run, and test commands from project files. List environment variable names only. Do not execute commands; mark them unverified.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Trace a Central Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace [request, command, or event] from entry to storage or output. List files and functions in order, cite evidence, and label inferences.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Prepare an Ownership Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an onboarding map of [repository]. Include one central flow, external services, quality signals, recent churn, and open questions. Review commands before requesting execution approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning maintenance after a project handoff

output_examples.input: Show the expected outline for a repository onboarding summary.
output: Purpose: project problem and intended users.
How to run: discovered commands and verification status.
Reading order: three inspected files with reasons.
Open questions: details not established from available evidence.

output_examples.input: What should a central-flow explanation include?
output: Entry: the inspected request handler, command, or event consumer.
Processing: relevant functions in execution order, with file references.
Data boundary: storage or external service calls found in the inspected code.
Result: the response or output, with any unverified behavior identified.

best_practices: Specify the repository and one central workflow to keep the map focused.
Review repository commands and hooks before approving execution in an isolated environment.
Require file references, verification status, and explicit labels for inferred behavior.
anti_patterns: Running unfamiliar installation, test, or lint commands without review or isolation.
Including secret values when configuration variable names are sufficient.
Treating a concise onboarding map as exhaustive documentation or a completed security audit.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: A concise onboarding map covering purpose, setup, structure, one central flow, dependencies, reading priorities, and open questions.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Repository access and command permissions depend on the host environment.

faq.question: Does it execute project commands?
faq.answer: The instructions call for running inexpensive tests and lint checks. Review commands first and isolate execution when the repository is untrusted.

faq.question: How does it handle environment secrets?
faq.answer: It explicitly prohibits printing secret values from environment files or configuration. Reports should list variable names only.

faq.question: Will it explain every file?
faq.answer: No. It prioritizes a two-level directory map, key entry points, and one central flow instead of an exhaustive file tour.

faq.question: How does it handle missing evidence?
faq.answer: Claims must cite inspected files. Inferences receive labels, unexecuted commands remain unverified, and unresolved details become open questions.
